title: Spartathlon 2026 Road Book — 26–27 September 2026
claims: The 2026 road book describes a point-to-point race from Athens to Sparta, reaching a maximum elevation of 1,200 m over paved roads, dirt roads and mountain trails.
The road book places aid stations approximately every 3,500 m, with food, water, refreshments and runners' personal supplies.

The 2026 road book lists 76 checkpoints numbered 0–75; checkpoint 0 is the Acropolis start at 07:00 and checkpoint 75 is the statue of King Leonidas in Sparta with a 19:00 closing time on 27 September.
The final checkpoint is km 244.74, giving a 36-hour race duration from the 07:00 start to the 19:00 close.
The road book lists cut-off times for every checkpoint and states that a runner arriving after the closing time will not be permitted to continue.
The road book describes doctors, physiotherapists and ambulances available throughout the 36-hour event, and a police and medical supervision system.

Basic aid-station provisions include water, Coca-Cola, juices, raisins, fruit, bread, biscuits, milk, coffee, potato chips, toast crackers, chocolate, sugar, honey, nuts and pasteli; main checkpoints add light meals, with soup and tea at many later points.

The road book marks assistance at selected checkpoints, including Elefsina, Megara, Isthmia, Ancient Corinth, Nemea, Lyrkeia, Mountain Base, Nestani, Tegea and Sparta; runners should use the assistance column rather than assume every checkpoint allows crew.

verification.note: Official 2026 road book PDF, 8 pages; text extracted and checkpoint table read.
